name: Sintered Rare-Earth (NdFeB) Permanent Magnets: India's REPM Scheme Award
scope: NdFeB magnets for EV traction motors, wind turbines, robotics and defence are ~90% China-sourced, and India's Rs 7,280 cr REPM scheme (6,000 MTPA, five winners of up to 1,200 MTPA each) drew 20 bids by 12 Aug 2026 with technical bids opened 13 Aug and awards still pending, so winner selection is the near-term catalyst; the theme is already PARTLY DISCOVERED (broker/retail 'rare earth stocks' pieces since 2025, Sona Comstar and GMDC well covered), so the earlier angle is the small/mid-cap bidders (20 Microns, Midwest) whose participation is thinly covered.
questions: What is a sintered NdFeB permanent magnet, what are its end markets (EV traction motors, wind, industrial/robotics, defence), and what is driving demand growth and China export-licensing risk now?

How does the Rs 7,280 cr REPM scheme work (6,000 MTPA, five beneficiaries up to 1,200 MTPA each, capital subsidy plus sales-linked incentive, 2-year build + 5-year incentive), and what is the expected award timeline after the 13 Aug 2026 technical bid opening?

Which Indian listed companies are confirmed bidders or have publicly stated plans (20 Microns, Midwest Ltd/Midwest Advanced Materials group, Coal India, L&T, Sona Comstar, others)? Verify each against exchange filings, scheme notices and company statements, and flag any bidder whose listing status or magnet link is unclear.

What are the capacity, capex, technology partners and timelines of each named company (e.g. Midwest Advanced Materials' Hyderabad NdFeB plant, Sona Comstar's in-house magnet plan), and how credible is execution given none has made sintered magnets at scale in India?

What is the upstream feedstock picture (NdPr oxide, monazite/REE mining and separation) and what are IREL, GMDC, Hindustan Zinc and others doing, since magnet makers need non-Chinese oxide and metal supply?
Which listed companies are customers who benefit from localisation (EV/auto component makers, motor and wind makers), and how exposed are they to imported magnet price and availability?

How much of this has the market already priced in: share-price performance over 3, 6 and 12 months for each name, how much of the move is attributed to rare-earth news, and how much mainstream/broker 'rare earth stocks' coverage already exists?

How material is the magnet opportunity to each company's revenue and earnings (a tiny line item at Coal India or L&T versus potentially transformative for a small cap like 20 Microns), and what are the funding and dilution needs?

What are the key risks: scheme awards going to unlisted or foreign players (Lohum, NEO, Proterial), delays, Chinese price undercutting, technology and qualification hurdles with auto OEMs, feedstock shortage?

What are the upcoming catalysts and what to watch: REPM award announcement, rare-earth corridors in Odisha/Kerala/AP/TN, ECMS magnet approvals, commissioning dates, OEM qualification wins and any new China export restrictions?

magnet_manufacturers: Smaller listed companies bidding for or building sintered NdFeB magnet capacity
auto_integrators: Large magnet importers with stated in-house production plans
conglomerate_bidders: Scale players that bid in the REPM scheme where magnets are a small line item
upstream_feedstock: Listed miners and state firms developing monazite/REE resources needed for magnets
